title: best-effort parse: malformed input yields warnings, not Err
description: parse() returns Err only for empty input and no-headers-at-all. Everything else — malformed headers, bad transfer encoding, encoding problems — produces a ParsedMessage with warnings populated. A future contributor might suggest converting more parse-time anomalies into Err returns to 'fail fast'. That would be wrong for a MIME parser: real-world email contains enormous amounts of non-conforming content. A parser that returns Err on malformed input is useless as a mail client component. The only truly unrecoverable case is when there is nothing to parse at all. All other anomalies should be surfaced as warnings so the caller can decide what to do.
